candidates.note: Comparative evidence: DEDR 1818 lists Tamil kuḻi ‘pit, hole, hollow, cavity, depression, excavation’; Kannada kuḻi ‘hollow, hole, pit, grave’; Tulu guri / guḷi ‘hole, pit’. The dictionary reconstructs Proto-Dravidian *kuḻ-V ‘pit, hollow’. This supports the Dravidian comparison; exact fit for every sense of ಕಂದಕ should still be judged in context.

tamil.meaning: pit, hole, hollow, cavity, depression, excavation

editorial.note: Research addition. DEDR 1818 supports the cross-language root comparison. No Halegannada citation has been verified; no historical form is claimed.

candidates.note: Tulu iḷijārů is recorded with the meanings ‘a slope, slipperiness’; it is analysed in the DEDR entry with iḷi- ‘slip out or down, slide’ (DEDR 503) and jār- ‘slip, slide down’ (DEDR 2482). This is a direct Tulu lexical comparison, not evidence for a Proto-Dravidian compound or a verified Tamil cognate.

editorial.note: Research addition. The Tulu form is directly attested in DEDR; no Tamil, Proto-Dravidian compound, or Halegannada equivalent is asserted.

candidates.note: Comparative evidence: Tamil மூன்று (mūṉṟu), Kannada ಮೂರು (mūru), Tulu ಮೂಜಿ (mūji); Proto-Dravidian numeral reconstructed as *mūnṯu / *muHnṯu (DEDR 5052 is also cited for *muv / *mū). Old Kannada ಮೂಱು (mūṟu) is listed as a historical form, but a primary inscription/text citation remains to be added. Sources: DEDR 5052; Dravidian Numerals (2009); The Dravidian Languages, §4.4.1; comparative numeral references.
